messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from the API-key scoping RFC review — I'm leaning toward introducing resource-scoped API keys for some internal service workflows. Thoughts on the main tradeoffs?

sam: Short answer: helpful for least-privilege, but operational surface grows. Need rotation, discovery, and a smooth migration path. :thinking:

alex: Can you sketch the intended shape? resource-scoped like `project:123/model:abc:read` or token-per-resource?

maria: Exactly, two designs in mind: (A) single token with embedded resource ACLs (claims list), or (B) many short-lived tokens minted per-resource on demand.

priya: A vs B breakdown from infra POV: A = simpler on mTLS/gateway, caching introspection is easy. B = better compromise of blast radius but needs a minting service + caching + strong lifecycle.

jon: If we go A (claims list) we must guard token size explosion. If users attach hundreds of resources it's awful. Maybe support wildcard scopes and explicit deny?

maria: Good point. Proposal: support three scope shapes: global, scoped with resource patterns (prefix/wildcard), and ephemeral single-resource tokens. Keep default as project-scoped to avoid surprise.

alex: How would policy enforcement work? Gateway should only make allow/deny decisions with minimal roundtrips. We don't want every request hitting introspection.

priya: Suggestion: token carries compact bitset-ish claim for common rights + an optional `scopes_url` pointing to a signed, cacheable ACL blob. Gateway caches ACLs for X minutes, fallback to introspection.

maria: Example token payload idea (JWT-ish):
```
{
  "sub":"svc-ingest-1",
  "scope":"project:123:ingest",
  "acl_blob":"/acls/abcd1234",
  "exp":1690000000
}
```
Cache TTL 5m by default, configurable per-tenant.

jon: That lets us avoid huge tokens while keeping fast checks. But we need to design ACL blob signing and rotation. Who mints these blobs? key-broker? tokens service?

sam: Make minting part of the token service (authn). It writes signed blobs to blobstore with versioned IDs. Key rotation is then just re-sign on rotation; old blobs remain valid until TTL. Also need GC process.

alex: Can we reuse existing artifact storage (S3) + object signed metadata? Concern: cross-region latencies during cold starts. Gateway needs low tail-latency.

priya: Gateways must operate with local cache + fallback. On cold miss, we should allow an asynchronous warming path — serve on stale ACL if token age < 30s and schedule refresh. Need a risk assessment.

maria: Operational questions: How does this interact with our Dedicated/Private modes where customers may enforce no external blobstore calls? We must support fully-local ACLs (embed ACL in token) or a private blobstore option.

jon: For Private, default to embedding ACL or using the customer's internal blobstore endpoint. Document both and make blobstore endpoint overridable in tenant config.

alex: RBAC mapping: we'll keep role definitions in central policy engine. ACL blobs map to resolved permissions per resource to avoid evaluating high-level policies in the hot path. This is expensive at mint time but cheap at runtime.

maria: Nice. Migration plan idea: phase 1 = support ACL blobs + pattern scopes; phase 2 = mint ephemeral tokens for single-resource operations and SDK helpers; phase 3 = deprecate oversized claims in tokens.

sam: Metrics to track: token size distribution, cache hit ratio for ACLs by region, latency on cold ACL fetch, and incidence of fallback-to-introspection.

security-bot: Reminder: any change that increases token surface requires fresh threat modeling and SCA sign-off. See checklist: https://intra.redwood/security/token-changes-checklist

priya: UX: SDKs should expose a `mintScopedToken(resource, actions)` helper that requests ephemeral tokens; falls back to a longer-lived project token if minting fails. Keep dev ergonomics high.

maria: OK concrete asks: (1) agree on ACL-blob approach? (2) confirm gateway cache + stale-serve policy? (3) owners for mint service + blobstore GC?

alex: +1 to ACL-blob. Cache + stale-serve ok with limits (max 30s stale). I'll own gateway policy change.

jon: I can own mint service changes + GC design.

sam: I'll add infra notes for private deployments and signed-blobstore integration.

maria: Awesome — I'll draft an RFC follow-up with these decisions and link owners. Thanks all! :rocket:
